ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is a transition-state structure; the central atom has visible connections in four directions: upper left connected to O bearing a negative sign, lower left connected to R, lower right connected to Cl, and upper right connected to N3. There are also curved arrows in the figure, but the problem requires ignoring the arrows. Reasoning: According to the specified method, directly count non-hydrogen bonds. There are 4 visible single-bond connections external to the central atom, namely central atom–O, central atom–R, central atom–Cl, and central atom–N3. N3 as an azido group needs to be expanded, and internally contains two N–N bonds. Therefore the total number of non-hydrogen bonds = 4 + 2 = 6.

method.method_draft: Count the non-H bonds directly from the picture. The central atom has four visible single-bond connections: to O⁻, to R, to Cl, and to the N₃ substituent. Then expand the N₃ label as an azide unit, which contributes two additional N–N bonds. Add these: 4 external bonds + 2 internal azide bonds = 6 total bonds.

The graph therefore has 4 + 2 = 6 non-hydrogen bonds.
